_comment: Single source of truth for the oMLX admin console's design tokens. The web console and the macOS app both read the generated artifacts, never this file directly. Regenerate with `python omlx/admin/build_tokens.py`; CI drift is caught by tests/test_design_tokens.py.

semantic._comment: Apple system colors, expressed per appearance so the web console reads the same weight as the native app's status dots.

typography._comment: Six levels, no others. Nothing may render below the auxiliary step (12px); the enhanced-readability switch now only raises contrast, because the floor it used to enforce is the floor of the scale itself.

families.sans: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', 'PingFang SC', 'Hiragino Sans GB', 'Noto Sans CJK SC', 'Microsoft YaHei', sans-serif
families.mono: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, 'SF Mono', Menlo, Consolas, monospace

aux.usage: captions, timestamps, table secondary cells, badges

body.usage: body copy, form labels, table primary cells

section.usage: section headings, drawer and sheet titles

space._comment: 8pt grid. 4pt exists only for icon-to-label gaps.

layout._comment: Grid metrics that are part of the layout scale rather than page-local numbers: the console measure (the dashboard layout default), the KPI card minimum width, the heatmap label column, the log viewer columns and row pitch, and the settings anchor rail. Every page shares the measure; the Status tab may widen it further with its own layout control.

material._comment: Two translucent layers only: the top bar and the modal scrim. Content surfaces stay solid.

elevation._comment: Micro shadows replace hard borders on cards and popovers.

badge._comment: Badge foregrounds. A tone badge is the system colour at 14% behind its label, which is far too light to carry text, so each appearance names the step that reaches 4.5:1 on its own tint (tests/test_admin_contrast.py measures it). The system colours stay for dots, bars and fills.

console._comment: Web console only: transition durations and the two overlay widths. The app animates with its own timings, so these never reach DesignTokens.swift.
